source_read: PMC HTML full text PMC4237191 (Drug Test Anal 2014;6(4):308-316, online 23 July 2013; title confirmed in my own tab): every section, Table 1 and Table 2 (all 129 rows checked programmatically in the page: category counts, the stated ratio rule, the 10% poisoning cut-off, N below 50 and internally impossible rows), article notes (received 4 March 2013, accepted 6 June 2013, CC BY-NC-ND) and the reference list. Figures 1 and 2: the screenshot of my tab came back blank, so the figure images were not viewable and no value was taken from them. The online supplement (a PDF) was not opened. No claims cite this source in this round; card check only.

key_findings.note: Forensic toxicology in Finland has two paragraphs and Data refining four on the page; the ICD-10 and ATC sentence is in Data refining, 3rd paragraph, as stated.
43,458/57,903 = 75.1%; 24,879/57,903 = 43.0%. The 8% and 15% are in Discussion, 6th paragraph.

Recounted from Table 2: 61 at 1, 22 below, 46 above; 46/129 = 35.7% (printed 35%). The editors' recount of 58, 23 and 48 is reproduced: risperidone 0.004/0.006 = 0.67, tizanidine 0.02/0.015 = 1.33, 4-methylaminophenazone 15/10 = 1.5. The ten largest ratios are listed correctly as printed, but two of them cannot be reproduced from the printed medians: amlodipine 0.07/0.015 = 4.7 (printed 4.5) and metformin 6/1 = 6.0 (printed 5.5). See missed.

Recounted 36 from Table 2. Methamphetamine, at exactly 10%, is rightly outside 'more than 10%'. The ten highest shares are correct (acebutolol, 20%, comes next). Figure 1 was not viewable for me either.

All 35 values checked against rows 13, 26, 42, 71, 79, 87 and 119. All seven ratios are printed as 1, and every median lies within its range (oxycodone at the upper limit). The fentanyl range comes from Winek et al. (footnote e), not Schulz.
All 55 values checked against the 11 rows named. Methamphetamine's range is printed '-0.1' (no lower limit), so 'up to 0.1' is an interpretation of that printed form.

key_findings.correction: The class ranges are the Discussion's (3rd paragraph), and Table 2 contradicts them. Trazodone, an antidepressant, has a ratio of 0.57, and dixyrazine, a phenothiazine antipsychotic, 0.33: both fall below the stated ranges for the other drugs of their class (antidepressants 1.2 to 4.7, antipsychotics 1.8 to 24). Mesoridazine (ratio 1) is also missing from the authors' list of antipsychotics at 1. Write 'the Discussion states ...' and add that by Table 2 the ranges are 0.57 to 4.7 for antidepressants and 0.33 to 24 for antipsychotics.
key_findings.note: The rest is confirmed. 'Most' neutral and acidic drugs within or below the range holds, with exceptions (phenazepam 2.1, gabapentin 1.8, pregabalin 1.6).
'20 drugs in common' comes from the Figure 2 caption. The figure image was not viewable for me either, so the 'very close' agreement rests on the authors' text.
0.07 mg/L is below the quoted toxic value of 0.088 mg/L, so the card's note stands. The paper frames the misreading as serious intoxication with impairment, not as a lethal level.

reporting_issues.note: Also: the mean must be at least 1.5 from the 95th percentile (30), and the mean lies below the median, against the Results' remark that means exceed medians. The printed ratio of 1.8 equals 0.90/0.5, so the median matches the ratio and the misprint more likely lies in the mean or the percentiles. Quetiapine is the only row that fails these bounds.
The printed 0.13 equals the median divided by the upper limit (0.10/0.8 = 0.125), which suggests the wrong limit was used.

I count 16 too. Nine of them (biperiden, bupivacaine, chloroquine, cyclizine, diclofenac, galantamine, pethidine, ropivacaine, sildenafil) belong to no method-restricted subset, which supports the card's reading that N counts quantified findings only.
Recomputed: men plus women 57,886; alcohol counts 24,878; pooled alcohol SD 1.11 (printed 1.16). Age pools to a mean of 54.6 and an SD of about 17.2 (printed 17.1), close enough.
Results says the relationships were plotted against the Vd midpoint, but no such plot is published.

risk_of_bias.note: I agree with the overall rating (editors' summary: moderate), and the JBI prevalence checklist fits a description of a measurement's distribution. Measurement quality is high; the bias lies in what the distributions are taken to represent (mixed causes of death, left-censoring at the LOQ, pathologists who knew the concentrations when certifying poisonings) and in misprints.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: 1. Sample frame appropriate to address the target population
2. Study participants sampled in an appropriate way
4. Study subjects and setting described in detail
5. Data analysis conducted with sufficient coverage of the identified sample
risk_of_bias_domains.note: Left-censoring could be filed under item 8 instead, but 'no' is defensible: a whole subgroup of detections (those below the LOQ) is left out of every distribution. Discussion, 3rd paragraph, adds that a majority of findings below the LOQ for some drug calls for a more sensitive method, which implies the omitted share is large for at least one drug.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: 6. Valid methods used for identification of the condition
7. Condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants

risk_of_bias_domains.note: The ratios that do not fit the printed medians (see missed) add a little to this domain's concerns.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: 9. Response rate adequate, or low response managed appropriately

interpretation_gap.note: Minor is fair: the abstract and Results are descriptive, and the overreach sits in the Conclusions. Two wording points for the card. (1) The Conclusions say the agreement is 'suggesting' that post-mortem reference concentrations apply internationally; the card's 'call ... applicable' drops that hedge. (2) results_show lists moclobemide among exceptions to the 'about 20 drugs in common', but the moclobemide difference comes from the comparison with Druid and Holmgren and Reis et al., not from the 20 drugs shared with Jones and Holmgren.

missed: Reporting issue: the Discussion's class ranges are contradicted by Table 2. Antidepressants other than fluoxetine are said to range from 1.2 to 4.7, but trazodone is 0.57. Antipsychotics are said to be 1 or from 1.8 to 24, but dixyrazine is 0.33, and mesoridazine (1) is left out of the list (Discussion, 3rd paragraph; Table 2, rows 35, 69 and 120).

Several printed ratios cannot be reproduced from the printed medians: amlodipine 0.07/0.015 = 4.7 (printed 4.5), metformin 6/1 = 6.0 (5.5), phenazepam 0.09/0.04 = 2.25 (2.1), betaxolol 0.10/0.05 = 2.0 (1.9). These were probably computed from unrounded medians. No category changes, so the counts stand, but cite ratios as printed and do not recompute them from the table.

How a case entered the data: the 57,903 cases average about 5,260 a year, against 'over 6,500' toxicology cases a year described for the system. The paper does not say which toxicology cases are missing from the femoral-blood dataset (for example bodies without femoral blood, or analyses that were not comprehensive), so deaths sampled differently may be excluded.
